 Sydney Kings Form 
 Sydney have won five of their last six matches, with every victory coming by eight points or more. The Kings have also dominated this matchup, winning eight of their last nine meetings against Cairns, giving them a strong case to cover the handicap. 
 Kendric Davis has been in excellent scoring form, producing 26 and 35 points in his last two appearances against the Taipans. With Sydney averaging a league-high 99.0 points per game, Davis is backed to continue leading the attack and reach 25+ points. 
 The Kings' team total also looks appealing. Sydney have averaged 112 points across their last three meetings with Cairns, while the Taipans concede 97.0 points per game this season. With the Kings finding their offensive rhythm, another triple-figure performance is expected.

 Cairns Taipans Form
 Cairns have struggled for consistency this season, sitting with a 7-6 record against the handicap despite showing signs of improvement in recent weeks. 
 The Taipans average 93.0 points per game while conceding 97.0, ranking sixth defensively. Their rebounding remains a concern, collecting just 35.3 boards per game, the lowest average in the competition. 
 Jack McVeigh has been a major offensive contributor and enters this contest after matching his career high with eight three-pointers in his previous appearance. Jaylon Brown has also been important, with Cairns winning all five games in which he has scored at least 15 points this season. 
 Sydney Kings Form
 Sydney have been one of the NBL's strongest teams, winning three consecutive matches and five of their last six to build an 8-3 record. 
 The Kings lead the league in scoring at 99.0 points per game while conceding just 89.1, the competition's best defensive record. Their ability to dominate both ends has been reflected in their recent victories, with each of their last five wins coming by at least eight points. 
 Davis has found his scoring touch, averaging 24 points and 9 assists in his last three games. Xavier Cooks has also been outstanding around the basket, leading qualified players in field goal percentage at 68.7%. 
 Sydney's combination of offensive firepower, defensive discipline and recent form makes them one of the toughest teams to beat in the competition.
